items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Each format pair has its own branch, which makes intent fairly clear. But the swizzle shuffle masks (e.g. `{12,13,14,15,-1,-2,...}`) have no comments, and short names like v0, v1, v_mid, b0..b3 are used throughout the kernels.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The packed swizzle function is one long if/else chain over format pairs (likely over 100 lines), with near-duplicate shuffle-plus-scalar-tail loops for each pair. Build artifacts (.zig-cache/*, zig-out/lib/libswscale_candidate.so) were committed in the diff.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Plane pointers are force-unwrapped with `src[0].?` and `dst[0].?`, which is undefined behaviour in ReleaseFast if a plane is null. Shuffle masks are bare magic numbers. The final edits left a regression (46/58 within the bars) that was never fixed, and the hidden correctness test failed.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: Kernels do have scalar tails (`while (i < w_u)`) and advance rows by stride. But after the unscaled.zig rewrite, the last check showed 12 conversions outside the bars, and the hidden correctness test failed, so some formats or geometries produce wrong pixels.
